page: OVHcloud b2-120 is a general-purpose server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Haswell processor with 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 120.0 GB of RAM, providing 3.75 GB of memory per core, alongside a local 400 GB SSD and a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance under stress-ng is categorized in the bottom 10%, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression is weak, falling in the bottom 25%. However, the multi-core CPU performance, passmark CPU score, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression all fall within the average range of the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks also demonstrate average performance.

This instance is suited for workloads that can leverage its 32 dedicated cores, such as multi-threaded database operations, static web serving, and moderate redis deployments, which both perform in the average tier. It is less suitable for single-threaded tasks or intensive LLM text generation, where it exhibits poor to weak performance. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers a high density of dedicated physical cores and a balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it a stable option for parallelized general-purpose workloads without the premium cost of newer architecture generations.
